title: Recursive shelves: Peak ticket
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Divide-and-conquer recursion. Return the largest number in the result list.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
readings is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless Step 1 says otherwise. k is included in the function call, but this task does not use it. You can ignore it.

Step 1: Build the result list
Start with the whole readings list as a section. Record the sum of that section. If it has more than one number, split it into a left half and a right half. Use the same steps on the left half first, then on the right half. When a section has an odd length, the left half has one fewer number. A section with one number is not split. Do not record empty sections. The result list contains the sums in the order you record them.

Step 2: Return the answer
Return the largest number in the result list. If the list is empty, return 0. If all numbers are negative, return the largest negative number; do not replace it with 0.

Write your function
Complete recursiveShelvesPeakTicket(readings, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.

constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n log n); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
